title: Governed LLM client (LangGraph)
blurb: Point LangGraph at your Omni Gateway proxy and get back a real langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI — credentials, correlation and cost headers injected. No wrapper to code around.
prompt: Tell me a one-sentence bedtime story about a unicorn.
watch: A normal answer streams back. The dev panel fills in a live Budget bar and one donkey.llm.chat span with donkey.policy.decision=allow.

# and nothing tells you the call went through governance.

model = ChatOpenAI(
    model="gpt-5.1",
    base_url=os.environ["DONKEY_LLM_PROXY_URL"],   # the Omni Gateway proxy
    api_key=os.environ["GATEWAY_TOKEN"],
)
reply = await model.ainvoke(messages)
# No correlation id, no budget, no span, no typed refusal.

# With DDK — the same ChatOpenAI, the same gateway, governed.

donkey = Donkey.from_env(team="support", project="triage")
model = donkey.langgraph.chat_model("gpt-5.1")   # real ChatOpenAI

async with donkey.run(id=ticket.id):
    reply = await model.ainvoke(messages)

print(donkey.budget.remaining)   # updated in-band from the response

title: Typed refusal — token budget (429)
blurb: On this proxy a 429 is a token-budget refusal, never retried. TokenBudgetExceeded carries .retry_after so you pace, not hammer.
prompt: Summarise this 400-page contract in exhaustive detail.
watch: TokenBudgetExceeded surfaces with retry_after. DDK never auto-retries a 429 — retrying only earns the same refusal.
with:
# With DDK — same messages, same model; a 429 is a terminal budget refusal.
from donkey_kit import TokenBudgetExceeded

try:
    reply = await model.ainvoke(messages)
except TokenBudgetExceeded as e:
    await asyncio.sleep(e.retry_after)   # wait for the window, then continue
    # transport already treats the 429 as terminal — no silent retry storm

title: Typed refusal — request rate limit (429)
blurb: The stock rate-limiting policy counts requests, not tokens. Its 429 is RequestRateLimitExceeded, with .retry_after read from x-ratelimit-reset, so it never looks like a token-budget 429. donkey.budget.requests tracks the window.

try:

except RequestRateLimitExceeded as e:
    await asyncio.sleep(e.retry_after)   # x-ratelimit-reset (ms), as seconds

title: Budget & pacing
blurb: The gateway's token window is a first-class Budget object. pace(reserve=) stops BEFORE the limit; wait_for_reset() resumes. An overnight batch slows down instead of dying at 2am.
prompt: Run a 6-call enrichment batch under a 5% reserve.
watch: fraction_used climbs call by call. If the reserve is crossed, BudgetReserveReached is raised before the request and the loop waits for reset — no wasted spend.
without:
# Without DDK — parse the ratelimit header by hand at every call site,
# and most code skips it until the first 429 crashes the job.
for record in batch:
    reply = await model.ainvoke(messages_for(record))
    hdr = reply.response_metadata["headers"].get("x-llm-proxy-ratelimit", "")
    remaining = int(re.search(r"(\d+) tokens remaining", hdr).group(1))  # brittle
with:
# With DDK — never parse a header; pace the same loop.
for record in batch:
    async with donkey.budget.pace(reserve=0.05):   # raises at 95%
        reply = await model.ainvoke(messages_for(record))

# recover cleanly at the window boundary:
except BudgetReserveReached:
    await donkey.budget.wait_for_reset()

title: Step-up approval pending (CIBA)
blurb: With CIBA on the OAuth2 OBO policy, a 401 authorization_pending becomes GatewayApprovalPending with .retry_after. It is not an AuthError telling you to rotate credentials the gateway just accepted.
prompt: Approve a $2,400 refund for order 1182 on behalf of the signed-in customer.
watch: Not interactive yet; a live version is planned via donkey-sim/ciba-pending. The 401 shape is VERIFIED (LIVE). It was captured on an A2A message/send behind OBO policy 1.1.3, not on an LLM proxy route. Pending is not a refusal, so no policy span attributes are set. The SDK re-sends only if you opt in with wait_for_approval(), and the gateway never reports an unanswered request as expired.
with:
# SDK shipped; descriptive example, not executed by this card.
from donkey_kit import GatewayApprovalPending
from donkey_kit.core.step_up import wait_for_approval

try:
    # re-sends after each retry_after (kept within 1-30s) until approved

title: Typed refusal — tool not in access profile
blurb: When the gateway's MCP Global Access or Attribute-Based Access Control policy refuses a tools/call, the response is HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC error -32008, not an HTTP error. DDK raises ToolNotInProfile naming the tool and server. It is a configuration problem and is never retried.

For other frameworks that raise the mcp error, tool_access_denial(exc) converts it. ADK and Strands return text, which the SDK does not classify. e.profile is always None, because the gateway names no rule.

blurb: donkey verify and Publication.verify() compare what a version was published with against what is live: an MCP server's tools/list, or the card an a2a_v1 agent serves, read through its governed gateway instance. Read-only. Drift warns by default; raise_on_drift=True raises PublicationDrift instead.

The reads it depends on were verified live: the Exchange read-backs of mcp-metadata tools and agent cards, and the agent's card through the gateway (2026-10-29), plus the governed MCP binding (2026-10-28). Parameter types are not compared, and neither are card fields that describe the deployment (url, version, security). Agents with protocol other are skipped, and API publications raise NotImplementedError.
without:
# A server changes after release and Exchange keeps advertising the old
# tools; nobody notices until an agent calls a tool that no longer exists.

from donkey_kit.experimental import Publication, PublicationAssetType

pub = Publication(asset_type=PublicationAssetType.MCP_SERVER, group_id="<group-id>",
                  asset_id="ddk-demo-sku-lookup", version="1.1.0",
                  name="SKU Lookup MCP Server", description="Looks up a SKU.")
drift = await pub.verify(donkey)                 # warns, returns the differences
await pub.verify(donkey, raise_on_drift=True)    # raises PublicationDrift

title: Tool filtering & token estimates
blurb: ToolSet.filter() narrows a set with allow/deny globs, predicates and servers=. Deny wins, and a later filter cannot bring back a tool an earlier one removed. describe() lists each server's tools. descriptor_tokens() then estimates their prompt cost after collision renames.
watch: Not interactive here. The filter logic is local. filter(servers=[...]) was used in the VERIFIED (LIVE) gateway binds (verified-apis §9, 2026-10-28), and it drops servers before any tool is listed. A name that matches no tool raises ConfigError once descriptors are known. The estimate is about four JSON characters per token, not a bill, and an unlisted server counts as zero. Filtering is not gateway authorization. Each bind also logs this estimate and warns above 20 tools or 10,000 tokens (see the descriptor cost warning card).
without: # Expose every descriptor and guess its model prompt cost.
with:
# SDK shipped; descriptive example, not executed by this card.

tools = await found.describe()          # tools/list on each server
narrow = tools.filter(allow=["get_*"]).filter(deny=["get_ssn"])
estimate = narrow.descriptor_tokens()   # ~4 JSON chars/token

title: Descriptor cost warning on bind
blurb: Every ToolSet binding logs how many tool descriptors it exposes and roughly how many prompt tokens they add to each model call. It warns once the set passes 20 tools or 10,000 tokens, the published vendor guidance, so a bloated tool set is caught before the model's tool selection degrades.
watch: Not interactive here. This is local logging on the bind path: a debug line on every bind and a warning above DONKEY_TOOL_WARN_COUNT / DONKEY_TOOL_WARN_TOKENS (0 turns one off). Token figures come from descriptor_tokens(), about four JSON characters per token and not a bill. A server whose descriptors are unknown counts as zero. To narrow the set, see the tool-filter-tokens card.
